thread:
jen_support: FYI customer in DE is seeing steady 200-300ms extra RTT and occasional 500s starting ~09:10 CET. They say endpoints route to us-west. Here's their curl, reproduced by them:
```
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' -d '{"model":"rwd-3","input":"hello"}'
```
Response shows Server: redwood-edge-us and X-Region: us-west-2, whereas customer IP geolocates to Frankfurt.

samir_netops: Can you paste their source IP (customer ok'd sharing?) and example traceroute? ISP caching often causes wrong POP for certain prefixes.

jen_support: Customer provided IP 85.214.23.56 and traceroute attached (short). They ran nslookup to api.redwood-inference.com -> A 34.98.12.77 (us). They say TTL on their resolver is 300 but looks sticky.

opsbot: Incident created #INC-2026-1427. Impact: 1 customer, production, elevated latency and 500s for auth. Autocategory: routing/dns.

elaine_sre: Quick checks: 1) did we recently update MaxMind/GeoIP DB or anycast announce changes? 2) any rollback of regional peering yesterday? 3) check our authoritative DNS NS config and EDNS responses.

luis_prodeng: We did a minor Anycast adjacency change in fra late weekend (announced more specific for some test prefixes). Not aware of DB updates. I'll check routeviews and our BGP announcements.

samir_netops: Meanwhile, ask customer to run: `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @<their_resolver> +trace` and `dig +short txt whoami.cloudflare.com` if they go through Cloudflare. Also `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8` so we can compare resolver-specific answers. Sticky ISP caches + EDNS stripping commonly cause wrong POP selection.

jen_support: Customer returned dig results: their ISP resolver returns us IP; 8.8.8.8 returns eu FRA IP. Traceroute shows first hop inside ISP then goes to us backbone. Customer says this started after weekend deploy. They also report a billing spike because requests charged at us model price.

elaine_sre: That pattern suggests resolver is returning stale A due to cache or the ISP is not honoring EDNS-Client-Subnet so we fall back to coarse geoip based on resolver IP. Workarounds: 1) suggest customer switch to public resolver as a test; 2) we can enable short-term sticky routing override for that customer IP to force eu POP.

luis_prodeng: Can we safely add a host-level route in the routing layer mapping 85.214.23.56 -> FRA pool? Needs engineering approval for one-off. If approved, we'll need an entry in routing config and a graceful rollback plan.

samir_netops: Also validate our GeoIP provider data. I see a possible mismatch for that /24 in our staging MaxMind snapshot from last Monday. If DB stale, update could fix larger set. I'll coordinate update and push to edges with safe TTLs.

jen_support: Customer wants ETA. I told them we'll follow up in 30m with either mitigation or workaround.

opsbot: @samir_netops assigned. SLA: 2 hours.

samir_netops: Action plan: (1) ask infra to push one-off route for the single IP to FRA (if approved) — takes ~15m; (2) refresh GeoIP DB globally — takes ~25-40m if no issues; (3) recommend customer temporary resolver change or DNS cache flush on their edge. I'll post updates here.

luis_prodeng: If we add one-off mapping, we'll annotate billing pipeline so token accounting uses eu pricing for those sessions to avoid charge disputes. Need finance sign-off but can tag as customer credit pending.

elaine_sre: Also add a short-lived fallback policy: if edge sees repeated auth failures + high lat, prefer local model variant for those client IPs. Not a full fix but reduces latency impact.

jen_support: Thanks. Customer confirmed they can try 8.8.8.8 test. They're on hold while we implement.

samir_netops: Pushing GeoIP refresh now, will post whether the target /24 maps to FRA after update.

samir_netops: Update: GeoIP refresh complete. Our lookup now maps 85.214.23.56 -> DE-FRA. Please ask customer to retry and `dig` again.

jen_support: Customer retried — now gets FRA IP and latency normal, 40ms. They confirm no more 500s. They're happy. Will keep monitoring and issue a small billing credit for the spike.

luis_prodeng: Filed follow-up ticket to add automated detection for resolver-only misroutes and a playbook to apply temporary per-customer routing.

opsbot: Incident #INC-2026-1427 resolved. Root cause: stale GeoIP mapping for a /24 combined with ISP resolver caching. Remediation: GeoIP DB refresh, temporary per-client routing, billing credit.

jen_support: Closing loop with customer and documenting repro steps in support KB. :white_check_mark:
